key_insight: UNITE unifies image tokenization and latent diffusion into a single end-to-end trainable autoencoder by using a Generative Encoder that shares weights to act as both tokenizer and latent generator, removing the need for separate tokenizer pretraining.
problem_solved: Current latent diffusion workflows require a staged pipeline—first training a tokenizer (or VAE) and then training a diffusion model in the frozen latent space—adding engineering complexity, suboptimal latent alignment, and slow iteration cycles.
method: Design an autoencoder (UNITE) where a Generative Encoder serves dual roles: producing discrete/continuous tokens and generating latents for denoising via weight sharing.
Train the encoder and latent diffusion denoiser jointly in an end-to-end fashion with combined reconstruction and diffusion objectives so latents are optimized for generation from the start.
Eliminate the separate tokenizer-pretraining stage, enabling tighter latent–denoiser coupling and simpler training pipelines.
impact: Makes latent diffusion models easier and faster to develop by removing staged training and improving latent alignment with the denoiser, lowering engineering overhead and accelerating research and deployment cycles.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: single UNITE autoencoder showing the Generative Encoder branching to both tokenization and latent denoiser (weight-sharing highlighted).
Workflow comparison: staged pipeline (tokenizer → frozen latents → diffusion) vs. UNITE end-to-end training (single loop).
Qualitative panel: example reconstructions and generations comparing staged vs. UNITE outputs to show fidelity/alignment.
Training curves / ablation: joint-loss vs. staged baseline (convergence speed or validation quality) to illustrate practical gains.
paper_title: End-to-End Training for Unified Tokenization and Latent Denoising
paper_authors: Shivam Duggal, Xingjian Bai, Zongze Wu, Richard Zhang, Eli Shechtman
